This is Hall’s famous result that the permanent-income hypothesis implies that consumption follows a random walk (Hall, 1978).

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Friedman's permanent-income hypothesis says consumption is determined by lifetime resources (permanent income), not period income; Hall's (1978) extension under quadratic utility and rational expectations gives the Random Walk result C_t = C_{t-1} + e_t where consumption-change innovations are unpredictable from any t-1 information.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Permanent Income Hypothesis and Consumption under Uncertainty
